draft.title: Gestalt principles
card: Gestalt principles describe how the brain groups separate parts of a visual scene into a whole. The whole is seen as more than its parts.
the brain separates an object (the figure) from its background (the ground).
the brain fills gaps in an incomplete shape, so we see a complete form.
items that look alike are grouped (similarity). Items that sit close together are grouped (proximity).
draft.remember: The brain groups visual parts into wholes, using cues such as gaps, likeness and nearness.

a.q: A poster shows a circle drawn with a few small gaps in its outline. Viewers still see a whole circle. Which principle explains this?
a.why: The brain fills the gaps in the outline so a complete shape is seen. This is closure. Proximity is about grouping items that sit close together, not about filling in missing parts.
a.clue: What does the brain do with the missing parts?

b.q: At a school assembly, Year 7 students in green jumpers sit scattered among students in grey jumpers. An observer sees the green jumpers as one group. Which principle explains this?
opts: Similarity, because the jumpers look alike
Proximity, because the students sit close together
Closure, because the gaps between students are filled
Figure-ground, because the hall is the background
b.why: The students are scattered, so they are not grouped by nearness. The observer groups them because their jumpers share a colour, which is similarity. Proximity is the tempting answer, but the green jumpers are not sitting close together.
b.clue: Are the green jumpers sitting close together, or just alike?

b.best: Similarity, because the jumpers look alike

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the VCE treatment of figure-ground, closure, similarity and proximity, and both questions have a single clear answer that the explanations confirm.
